Normalization


Save figure


Save figure
Save figure


Normalization method : each intensity is expressed relatively to a reference intensity, as a ratio of intensities. Intensities of the sample with the lowest number of missing values are used as reference intensities. Intensities are then centered by substracting the median of the ratios for each sample.


Missing values imputation


Save figure
Save figure


Save figure


Missing values are imputed with the noise model: values are drawn around the noise level of each sample (the 5% percentile of its observed intensities) with a standard deviation of 0.81 log2, estimated on 6701 low-intensity protein measurements within conditions. The imputation uses a fixed seed and is reproducible.


Dimension reduction


Save figure


Log10 intensities, each protein centered. Proteins vary in weight according to their variance, so the components reflect the largest changes between samples.

Save figure


Each protein is also scaled to unit variance, so all proteins weigh the same, including the many proteins that do not change. Their technical noise then has as much weight as the biological changes: this view helps to detect technical effects (injection order, batches), not biological ones.


Save figure


Sample scores of the main PCA against the number of proteins quantified in each sample. A strong correlation (|r| close to 1) means that the component mostly reflects differences in proteome depth (and therefore imputed values) rather than biology.
